Here is a precise breakdown of all three questions:

---

## 1. Where the `Proxy-Authorization` header is removed

The removal happens in [`rebuild_proxies()`](r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L318-L319) in [`src/requests/sessions.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py):

```python
# sessions.py, line 318–319
if "Proxy-Authorization" in headers:
    del headers["Proxy-Authorization"]
```

This is an **unconditional delete** — it runs regardless of where the header came from or whether a proxy is even in use.

---

## 2. What logic decides to strip it

`rebuild_proxies()` is called during redirect handling (in [`resolve_redirects()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L159)). The logic was introduced as a **security fix** (CVE addressed in 2.31.0) to prevent `Proxy-Authorization` headers from being forwarded through a CONNECT tunnel to the destination server.

The sequence is:
1. Any existing `Proxy-Authorization` in the request headers is deleted unconditionally.
2. The proxy URL is inspected for embedded credentials (`user:pass@proxy:8080`).
3. If credentials are found **and the scheme is not HTTPS**, a new `Proxy-Authorization` is reconstructed from those URL credentials.

```python
# sessions.py, line 326–329
# urllib3 handles proxy authorization for us in the standard adapter.
# Avoid appending this to TLS tunneled requests where it may be leaked.
if not scheme.startswith("https") and username and password:
    headers["Proxy-Authorization"] = _basic_auth_str(username, password)
```

For **HTTPS targets**, `Proxy-Authorization` is intentionally never set in the request headers — it is handled separately by urllib3 at the socket level via [`proxy_headers()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/adapters.py?L592-L611) in the HTTP adapter, which passes it out-of-band when establishing the CONNECT tunnel.

---

## 3. When the header is preserved vs. stripped

| Scenario | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Header set manually by user, HTTPS target | **Stripped** — deleted by `rebuild_proxies`, never re-added (urllib3 handles auth separately) |
| Header set manually by user, HTTP target | **Stripped then potentially replaced** — only if credentials are embedded in the proxy URL |
| Credentials embedded in proxy URL (`http://user:pass@proxy`), HTTP target | **Reconstructed** by `rebuild_proxies` from the URL |
| Credentials embedded in proxy URL (`http://user:pass@proxy`), HTTPS target | **Not set in headers** — passed to urllib3 via `proxy_headers()` in the adapter instead |

---

## Why your setup broke

Your code sets `Proxy-Authorization` manually in the headers dict and uses an HTTPS target:

```python
headers = {"Proxy-Authorization": "Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz"}
requests.get("https://example.com", headers=headers, proxies={"https": "http://proxy:8080"})
```

`rebuild_proxies()` deletes it unconditionally (line 318–319). Because the target is HTTPS, the re-add branch (`if not scheme.startswith("https")`) is skipped. The header never makes it to the proxy.

**Fix:** Embed credentials in the proxy URL instead of the headers:

```python
requests.get(
    "https://example.com",
    proxies={"https": "http://user:pass@proxy:8080"}
)
```

This is the only supported path for HTTPS proxy auth — `proxy_headers()` in the adapter will extract the credentials and pass them to urllib3 for use during the CONNECT handshake, where they are sent to the proxy (not leaked to the destination server).
